title: finding(types): the retire-vs-remove discriminator is written out in full at SIX sites across two files, so every amendment is an N-site hand edit — objectui#9682 amended five and missed the sixth
body:
Found during the in-seat review of PR objectui#9682 (card objectui#7678). That card exists because two statements of one rule disagreed. Fixing it required editing **five** of them, and the review found a **sixth** the fix did not reach.

## Measured

The retire-vs-remove discriminator — *"a `?: never` tombstone is available only on a surviving carrier; on one, tombstone when either prong holds: (1) steer authors to a named live replacement KEY, or (2) keep loud a key the docs taught as working"* — is written out in full at **six** separate sites across two files. Measured on PR objectui#9682's head `dce4a74a1`:

| file | site | retirement it argues | carries the amended precondition? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `complex.ts` | ~`:161`–`:174` | `KanbanColumn.color` | ✅ (amended by objectui#9682) |
| `complex.ts` | ~`:1059`–`:1065` | `ChatbotSchema` dark keys | ✅ (amended by objectui#9682) |
| `complex.ts` | ~`:1392`–`:1400` | `displayMode` | ✅ (was already the model) |
| `complex.ts` | ~`:1878`–`:1885` | `triggerIcon` | ✅ (amended by objectui#9682) |
| `mobile.ts` | ~`:136`–`:145` | `MobileOverrides` | ✅ (amended by objectui#9682) |
| `mobile.ts` | ~`:305`–`:322` | `GestureConfig` / gestures | ⛔ **no** |

Probe: `grep -inE "surviving carrier|either prong holds|prong 1|prong 2"` over both files returns those six clusters. Lit control: the phrase resolves to zero hits outside them, so the count is the population and not a sample.

## Why this is a finding and not a tidy-up

⭐ **The duplication is the recurrence mechanism, and this card is the second occurrence, not the first.** objectui#7678 was filed because `complex.ts` and `mobile.ts` stated contradictory rules. The rule was then amended once (objectui#7678's own comment `5548730153`, adding the surviving-carrier precondition), and the amendment had to be applied by hand at five sites. One was missed — in `mobile.ts`, the very file whose contradiction started the card.

⇒ Each future amendment is an N-site edit where N grows with every retirement, and the failure mode is silent: the sites do not reference each other, so nothing goes red when they drift. The only thing that has ever caught the drift is a human reading two of them side by side.

## Cost

An author or agent landing on `mobile.ts:305` today gets the **un-amended** two-prong rule and no precondition, and will conclude that a whole exported type name is a tombstone candidate — which is exactly what the amendment exists to deny.

## Shape of the remedy — ⛔ not decided here

One named block that the others cite, so the next amendment is a one-site edit. ⚠️ That is a **structural** change to published JSDoc (comments in this package reach the published `.d.ts`), not a prose fix, so it wants its own grading: a reader who follows a citation out of the block they are in pays a jump, and whether that trade is right is the question this card asks rather than answers.

⛔ This card does not propose deleting any of the six. Five of them add a per-retirement argument (*which* prong holds, and why) that a shared block cannot carry.

## Not measured

⛔ Whether the same shape exists for any other rule in `packages/types` — only this discriminator was enumerated. ⛔ Whether `mobile.ts:305`'s un-amended copy has actually misled anyone yet; unlike objectui#9681, no instance is claimed here. ⛔ What a shared block would cost a `.d.ts` consumer reading the published declarations.

Refs: objectui#7678 (the contradiction that started it) - PR objectui#9682 (the five-site amendment) - objectui#5941, objectui#7526 (the precedent changesets the rule is quoted from) - objectui#7519 (where one prong-2 judgement is recorded rather than decided).
